Happy New Year Reddit!

It's time for New Year's Resolutions. So allow me to share one of mine.

In 2016, I want to make sure Reddit expands upon its reputation as a free and open place to exchange ideas. Not just for those of us in the typical-redditor demographic, but for everyone else as well.

I'm a little concerned that over the last few years, and especially the last few months, that reputation is starting to erode. I'm seeing an increase in complaints from users that some of our larger communities are turning into echo chambers, where unpopular opinions are not tolerated. In 2016, that will no longer be the case.

We're going to fix this by clarifying a few recent policy changes, and shifting a lot of the power currently held by moderators into the hands of typical redditors. So let's start with a list.

1. Our community manager will review the rules of larger subreddits. Rules that exist just to quash certain viewpoints will be removed, or alternatively, the subreddit will be renamed to clarify that it is pro or against a particular set of ideas. We will engage directly with each community, by creating discussion threads at pre-announced times, during this process.

2. Moderators will now be accountable to the community for their moderation. Moderators who do not apply the published subreddit rules fairly and consistently will be removed by our community manager. This applies to all subreddits.

3. From now on, you are always free to complain about moderation policies in every subreddit, without fear of getting banned. Feel free to PM our community manager a link to the thread if we need to get involved. Moderators who censor criticism of themselves will promptly be removed.

4. Posts removed by mods will be accessible via a removed tab (just like the new tab) for all subs. You can upvote and downvote inside removed - posts are sorted the same way as in the normal subreddit. Illegal content can be flagged for removal by an admin.

5. We're bringing back /r/reddit.com, so redditors will have a place to discuss issues that effect the entire site, and anything else that can't be pigeonholed. /r/reddit.com is a default sub with no rules beyond those which apply to the entire site.

**About harassment, bullying, and the recent subreddit bans.**

Harassment is still, and always will be, against the rules of Reddit. We are defining harassment as following a user around and verbally abusing them, or trying to track them down and communicate with them outside reddit for unfavorable purposes. In other words, if a Redditor wants to ignore you, and you take steps to make yourself impossible to ignore, you're harassing them. This will get you a swift sitewide ban.

Saying mean things about a user - even frequent mean things over an extended period of time - is criticism, not harassment, and allowed. For example, you are allowed to create /r/redditsceosucks and post bad things about me all day. But following me around and calling me names in every comment I post, over time, would be harassment.

Under this mindset, we are reversing all community bans and restrictions except those which created legal challenges that threatened the existence of Reddit.

**About moderators**

Reddit appreciates that moderators are volunteers who have invested uncountable hours into helping reddit grow. However, the personal sense of ownership many moderators feel over their communities is also driving users away, and holding Reddit back.

Reddit is, and always will be, about the users - not the admins, and not the moderators. We need to make sure everyone is on board with that philosophy.

If any subreddits are taken private, deleted, or otherwise vandalized in protest of these new policies, the changes will be immediately reversed, and the account responsible will be banned.

**Let us know**

We're looking forward to hearing from everyone, in the comments of this post, and in /r/reddit.com, about the new policies and the direction we're going.

Remember, the big goal here is to make sure that Reddit remains a place where everyone can come to share links and discuss ideas - not just those of us who are in positions of power, or happen to share the same views as those who are.
